spatial_claims.claim: AB is a straight line and C is a point on segment AB, creating segments AC and CB
Prop 2.4 applied to line AB cut at C: sq(AB) = sq(AC) + sq(CB) + 2*rect(AC,CB)
Prop 2.3 applied to line AB cut at C: rect(AB,BC) = rect(AC,CB) + sq(BC)

configuration_map: Single straight line AB with one interior point C. Segments: AC (from A to C) and CB/BC (from C to B). No auxiliary points, no triangles, no circles, no angles. All constructed objects are areas (squares and rectangles) derived from these segments. Both Prop 2.3 and 2.4 are applied to the identical configuration of line AB cut at C.
skip_reason: The proof is purely algebraic. It applies two Book 2 algebraic identities (2.3 and 2.4) to the same line-cut-at-a-point configuration, then performs equation manipulation using Common Notions. There are no geometric configuration claims (no angles, no interior/exterior positions, no ray orderings, no constructions beyond the given line segment). No spatial contradiction is possible in a purely algebraic argument.
